chapter: New York, Henderson and Charlie Johnson
title: Bobby Stark, the underrated trumpeter
summary: Autrey calls Bobby Stark, a Wilberforce graduate with Chick Webb, one of the most underrated trumpeters; perhaps he was too nice.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Well being such a musician he was, and now, meeting the guys, and getting the guys, somebody sent me. He didn't ask me. Somebody said well Fletcher needs a trumpet player. And he said go over there and tell him I sent you. Or just go there. One of those things. I happened to walk in. I was glad, and Fletcher was glad. Now whether -- he had people like Bobby Stark Stocks. Oh, no greater trumpet player ever lived than Bobby.
And that's a man who has very little been mentioned, one of the most underrated trumpet players I think in the country. Bobby Stark Stocks (sic) was a heck of a trumpet player.
I don't know. I don't know. Nobody mentioned him. He was with Chick, and he was -- and he could play, and did play, and a heck of a nice guy, a gentleman.
Was he too nice a guy? Was that his problem?

I -- well maybe. Buy then I mean you know, maybe had he been one of those guys who was a knock-down drag-out like me, Sandy, and a whole other cats, maybe he would have been better off, maybe. But -- I dare anybody now to bring out a recording that he's on and they can tell me they do not like him. Because he was just that good, and he's a college graduate. I think he went to Fisk. No, not Fisk, he went to the other place in Ohio, the other college in Ohio.
Wilberforce. Yeah. And he's a doggone good man. You know?
